headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: ctx can read/write files and observe Claude Code events while Dify has broad networked tool execution and shared datastore state.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and can read filesystem content, while Dify wires tools into agent/workflow flows. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if ctx ingests Dify-produced text as trusted content. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ctx parses Dify-generated text or files as instructions without provenance checks
IF Dify outputs are copied into ctx-observed files or event streams
mitigations: Add provenance tags to Dify outputs before ctx ingests them
Restrict ctx to allowlisted file paths only
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text
Review one sample end-to-end prompt path for injection markers
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and filesystem content; Dify handles knowledge-base files, conversation logs, and model-provider API keys. If they share a workspace or Dify ingests ctx-managed files, sensitive data can flow into Dify's networked model/tool calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments and the blast radius includes secrets.
conditions: IF ctx-managed logs or graph data are placed in Dify-uploaded knowledge files
IF Dify sends those files or conversation context to external model providers
mitigations: Keep ctx and Dify on separate workspaces
Exclude logs and graph data from Dify uploads
Rotate any API keys exposed to Dify workflows
Audit one Dify workflow for outbound file/context transmission
requires-engineering: enforce tenant/workspace isolation and secret redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can write the filesystem and Dify can execute shell commands and write filesystem content, so both can mutate shared state if pointed at the same directory. Dify explicitly supports shared state via its datastore across instances, while ctx supports multiple instances, making write contention plausible even though Dify cannot modify git state. This is a real overlap but not the highest-risk git-lock scenario.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory or datastore
IF ctx hooks and Dify workflows run concurrently on shared artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Disable concurrent runs during shared edits
Check for overlapping paths before launch
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and Dify can route tool outputs into agent/workflow actions. If ctx-generated summaries or facts are fed into Dify without verification, Dify may act on them as authoritative. The pairwise chain is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate rather than low.
conditions: IF Dify workflows consume ctx summaries as trusted inputs
IF downstream Dify tools act on those summaries without a human review step
mitigations: Require human approval before Dify actions
Add a verification step for ctx-derived claims
Mark ctx outputs as untrusted metadata
Test one workflow with a deliberately wrong ctx summary
requires-engineering: implement confidence gates before action tools

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and graph data, while Dify stores conversation logs and knowledge-base files. If the same regulated data class is routed through both, retention and residency policies can diverge. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so this is a policy-alignment risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in both ctx logs and Dify conversation or knowledge-base storage
IF the two systems have different retention or deletion settings
mitigations: Inventory which regulated data each system stores
Align retention settings across both systems
Exclude sensitive records from one side
Verify deletion on a test record in each system
requires-engineering: add centralized retention and residency controls
